title: The Reality that will surely come.
subtitle: A name for the Day that cannot be avoided

row.title: it will surely happen
sub: promise and threat both come true

then: The surah opens with one word. Ibn Kathir says {idea}al-Haqqah is one of the names of the Day of Judgment{/idea}, because on it {idea}the promise and the threat will inevitably occur.{/idea} This was one of the earliest surahs in Makkah.
now: Your calendar is full of things that might happen. The trip, the interview, the wedding. {trap}Many will not go as planned.{/trap} {idea}One date is certain, though no one knows when.{/idea}
old: The Day of Judgment is something far off and vague.
new: It is the one event in my future that is completely certain.
try: Look at your plans for this week and add one thing you would do if you remembered that Day.

title: What is the Inevitable Reality?
subtitle: A question asked to make you stop
then: The word comes again, now as a question. Ibn Kathir says {idea}Allah declared the greatness of this matter.{/idea} Repeating it makes the listener in Makkah {reward}stop and wonder{/reward} before anything is explained.
now: A doctor sits down and says, we need to talk about your results. You stop scrolling. {idea}Some questions are meant to make you put everything down.{/idea} This is one of them.
old: I already know what the Day of Judgment is.
new: The question is asked so I stop and take it seriously again.
try: Sit for one minute today with no phone and ask yourself: what is that Day, for me?

title: What could make you truly know what it is?
subtitle: Something bigger than your imagination
then: The third line deepens the question: {idea}and what will make you know what al-Haqqah is?{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains it is said to {idea}declare the greatness of this matter.{/idea} Then the surah begins to show it, through the nations that denied it.
now: You have seen storms on the news and felt a hospital wait. You think you can picture big things. {idea}This Day is bigger than any of it.{/idea} The verse humbles your imagination.
old: I can imagine what that Day will be like.
new: It is greater than anything I can picture, so I listen to what Allah tells of it.
try: Read the next few verses of this surah slowly, as if hearing them for the first time.

title: Thamud and 'Ad called the Striking Day a lie.
subtitle: Two strong nations who denied what was coming
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah then mentions {trap}the destruction of the nations that denied the Resurrection.{/trap} Thamud and 'Ad were strong peoples of the past. {idea}Their denial did not change what was real.{/idea}
now: You ignore the dentist's warning. You do not open the bill. {trap}Not looking feels like it makes it go away.{/trap} {idea}It does not, and the same is true of bigger things.{/idea}
old: If I do not think about it, it is not my problem yet.
new: Denying something does not stop it. Preparing does.
try: Open one thing you have been avoiding, a message or a bill, and take one step on it.

title: Thamud was ended by an overwhelming blast.
subtitle: Transgression that brought its own end
then: Qatadah said the overpowering thing was {trap}the shout{/trap} that silenced them. Mujahid and others said it means {trap}their sins and transgression.{/trap} Ibn Zayd pointed to another verse: Thamud denied through their transgression.
now: A habit grows from one night to every night. A temper that was once a flash becomes the whole house. {trap}What we allow to grow can become what overwhelms us.{/trap} {idea}It is easier to stop it small.{/idea}
old: Disasters come from outside, not from what I do.
new: Unchecked wrongdoing can be the very thing that brings ruin.
try: Name one small habit that is growing in the wrong direction. Cut it back once today.

title: 'Ad was ended by a cold, raging wind.
subtitle: A strong people undone by the air
then: Ad-Dahhak said sarsar means {trap}cold{/trap}, and 'atiyah means it blew fiercely {trap}without any mercy or blessing.{/trap} The Prophet ﷺ said he was helped by an easterly wind, and 'Ad were destroyed by a westerly one.
now: You feel safe behind your walls, your insurance, your strong body. Then one storm, one virus, one night changes everything. {idea}Even the wind is under Allah's command.{/idea}
old: I am strong enough to handle whatever comes.
new: My strength is borrowed. The same air I breathe is in Allah's hands.
try: Next time you feel the wind today, remember who sends it and say alhamdulillah for safety.

title: Seven nights, eight days, and the mighty fell like trunks.
subtitle: How long it lasted and what was left
then: Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas and others said the days came {trap}in succession{/trap}, one after another. Ibn Abbas said hollow means {trap}ruined.{/trap} The people who had boasted of their strength {idea}lay like empty palm trunks.{/idea}
now: The tallest tower, the strongest company, the person everyone feared. {trap}Height and strength can be hollow inside.{/trap} {idea}What stands is what is rooted in Allah.{/idea}
old: Being big and strong means I will last.
new: Strength without faith can be hollow, however tall it stands.
try: Think of one way you show off strength. Replace it today with one quiet act of humility.

title: Do you see any of them left?
subtitle: A people gone without a trace
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}do you find any one of them left{/trap}, or anyone who even claims to be from them? {trap}They are all gone{/trap}, and Allah left them no successors.
now: Search an old social network you used ten years ago. Most of it is gone. Names, pictures, fame. {trap}Things vanish faster than we think.{/trap} {idea}What you send ahead to Allah does not.{/idea}
old: People will remember me and what I built.
new: Names fade. What lasts is what I did for Allah.
try: Do one good deed today that you will never mention to anyone.

title: Pharaoh and the overturned cities came with the same sin.
subtitle: Different nations, one shared error
then: Ibn Kathir says al-khati'ah means {trap}their rejection of what Allah revealed.{/trap} Ar-Rabi' said it means disobedience. Pharaoh's people and {trap}the cities that rejected their messengers{/trap} all shared it.
now: Different people, different lives, the same root: I know better than what Allah said. {trap}It shows up in a boardroom, a bedroom, a group chat.{/trap} {idea}Check your own heart for the root, not just the branches.{/idea}
old: My mistakes are all separate little things.
new: Many wrongs grow from one root: putting my view above Allah's word.
try: Pick one area where you quietly think you know better than Allah. Ask Him for humility in it.

title: They disobeyed their messenger, and the seizure was severe.
subtitle: Rejecting one messenger is rejecting them all
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}they all denied the messenger sent to them.{/trap} Only one messenger came to each nation, yet {idea}whoever denies a messenger denies all of them.{/idea} Mujahid said rabiyah means severe.
now: You hear a hadith you do not like and wave it off. You skip the part of the message that is inconvenient. {trap}Picking and choosing feels small.{/trap} {idea}The message is one whole.{/idea}
old: I can accept the parts I like and ignore the rest.
new: The message comes as a whole. Rejecting part of it is serious.
try: Find one teaching you have been avoiding. Learn one thing about why it was given.

title: When the flood rose, We carried you in the ship.
subtitle: Every human alive descends from the saved
then: Ibn Kathir says the water {trap}rose over its shores and overcame all that existed{/trap}, except those with Nuh in the ship. So {reward}all humans are from the loins of Nuh and his progeny.{/reward} That is why Allah says: We carried you.
now: You are here because, long ago, a few people were saved in a boat. Every person in your family tree survived something. {reward}Your existence is the end of a long chain of rescues.{/reward}
old: The flood is a story about other people.
new: I am alive because Allah carried my ancestors. It is my story too.
try: Thank Allah today for one specific ancestor or elder whose survival made your life possible.

title: A reminder for ears that hold on to it.
subtitle: Hearing that keeps what it hears

row.title: in one ear, out the other

then: Ibn Kathir explains that Allah {reward}caused ships to remain for you{/reward}, so you ride the water and remember His blessing. The story is told so that {idea}a conscious ear would hold on to it.{/idea}
now: You board a ferry, see a cargo ship on the news, take a plane over the sea. {idea}Each one can be a small reminder of the ark.{/idea} You hear many reminders a day. {trap}Most slip away.{/trap}
old: I have heard these stories so many times already.
new: The goal is not to hear more, but to keep what I hear.
try: Pick one verse from today and repeat it to yourself three times before bed.

title: One blast of the Horn, and it begins.
subtitle: Allah's command needs no second time
then: Ibn Kathir describes the blowings of the Horn: of fright, of destruction, then {idea}of standing before the Lord of all that exists.{/idea} It is called one blowing because {idea}the command of Allah cannot be opposed{/idea} and does not need repeating.
now: Your alarm rings and you hit snooze three times. Your mother calls you for dinner five times. {trap}We are used to second chances to get up.{/trap} {idea}On that Day, one call is enough for everyone.{/idea}
old: I will respond when the call gets serious.
new: When Allah calls, there is no snooze. Better to answer His calls now.
try: Get up for the next adhan on the first call, without waiting.

title: Earth and mountains lifted and leveled in one blow.
subtitle: The firmest things are not permanent
then: Ibn Kathir says the earth and mountains {trap}will be stretched out to the extent of the surface{/trap}, and {idea}the earth will change into something other than the earth.{/idea} All of it in a single crushing.
now: You say solid as a rock. You buy land because land lasts. Your house sits on ground you never think about. {trap}Even mountains are temporary.{/trap} {idea}Build on what does not end.{/idea}
old: Some things in this world are permanent.
new: Even mountains will be leveled. Only Allah and what is for Him remains.
try: Next time you see a hill or a tall building today, remember it is temporary and say subhanAllah.

title: On that Day, the Event will have happened.
subtitle: The waiting is over
then: After the Horn and the leveling, the verse says the Event {idea}will occur{/idea}, and Ibn Kathir explains it means {idea}the Day of Judgment.{/idea} The deniers of Makkah who said it would never come would see it.
now: You keep saying I will start next month. Next Ramadan. When things calm down. {trap}There will be a day when there is no next.{/trap} {idea}That Day is called the Event.{/idea}
old: There is always more time to get ready.
new: The Event will come as surely as if it already happened.
try: Take one good thing you keep postponing and start a small piece of it today.

title: The sky will split, weak and torn that Day.
subtitle: The roof over the world gives way
then: Ibn Jurayj linked this to another verse: {idea}the heaven shall be opened, it will become as gates.{/idea} Ibn Abbas said {trap}the sky will be torn apart{/trap}, and the Throne will be near it.
now: You look up from the bus stop and the sky is just there, blue or grey, always. {idea}It holds because Allah holds it.{/idea} One day He will let it open.
old: The sky is just the background of my life.
new: The sky stays whole by Allah's command, and one day it will open.
try: Look up at the sky once today for ten seconds and remember Who holds it.

title: Angels at the edges, and eight bear the Throne.
subtitle: The scene of the Lord's court

row.title: the angels
sub: on the sides of the sky

then: Ar-Rabi' said the angels will stand {idea}on the sides of the heavens, looking at the people of the earth.{/idea} Eight angels will carry the Throne. The Prophet ﷺ said of one of them: {idea}between his earlobe and shoulder is seven hundred years of travel.{/idea}
now: You have stood in a big airport, a stadium, a grand hall, and felt small. {idea}That Day's scene makes all of it nothing.{/idea} You will be standing in it too.
old: I am the center of my own world.
new: Before the Throne and its angels, I am small, and that is the right size.
try: In your next sujood, remember the greatness of the One you bow to.

title: Presented before Allah, with nothing hidden.
subtitle: No secret stays secret that Day
then: Ibn Kathir says you will be presented to {idea}the Knower of secrets and private counsels{/idea}, from Whom none of your affairs are hidden. The Prophet ﷺ said people will be shown three times: {trap}twice with arguing and excuses{/trap}, then the records fly into their hands.
now: Your search history. The deleted messages. The thought you never said out loud. {trap}You might have an excuse ready for each.{/trap} {idea}That Day, excuses run out and only the record speaks.{/idea}
old: I can always explain myself later.
new: Nothing is hidden from Allah, so I live now as if my record is open.
try: Delete or stop one thing in your private life you would not want shown that Day.

title: Here, read my record! The joy of the right hand.
subtitle: So happy you want everyone to see
then: Ibn Kathir says, out of {reward}extreme pleasure{/reward}, he says to everyone: take my book and read it. The Prophet ﷺ said Allah will bring a servant close, make him admit his sins, then say: {reward}I concealed these for you in the world, and I forgive you today.{/reward}
now: Remember getting a great report card and showing everyone at home. Now imagine that, but forever. {reward}And not because you never failed.{/reward} {idea}Because Allah covered and forgave.{/idea}
old: Only people with spotless records will be happy that Day.
new: Joy that Day can come from Allah's covering and forgiveness of my faults.
try: Ask Allah tonight: cover my faults in this world and forgive them on that Day.

title: I was certain I would meet my account.
subtitle: The belief that shaped a whole life
then: Ibn Kathir explains he means: {idea}I used to be certain in the worldly life that this Day would definitely come.{/idea} He links it to the verse about those {idea}certain that they will meet their Lord.{/idea}
now: You keep receipts because you know tax season comes. You study because the exam is on the calendar. {idea}The person who expects the account lives differently.{/idea} {reward}That certainty is what he is thankful for.{/reward}
old: I believe in the Day of Judgment, but it does not change my week.
new: Real certainty about meeting my account changes how I live today.
try: Before one decision today, ask: how will this look when I meet my account?

title: So he lives a life he is fully pleased with.
subtitle: Satisfaction that never wears off

row.title: the one who expected the account

then: Ibn Kathir says this life is {reward}pleasant.{/reward} After a life of being certain he would meet his account, the one with the right hand {reward}is now in a life he is fully pleased with.{/reward}
now: The new phone feels great for a week. The promotion for a month. {trap}Then the satisfaction fades and you want the next thing.{/trap} {reward}This verse describes a contentment that does not fade.{/reward}
old: If I get the next thing, I will finally be satisfied.
new: Lasting satisfaction is what Allah promises, not what the next purchase brings.
try: Notice one want today. Instead of buying, say: Allah, give me the life that truly pleases.

title: In a garden raised high.
subtitle: Paradise has levels far above each other
then: Ibn Kathir describes it as {reward}elevated, with pleasant stations and eternal joy.{/reward} The Prophet ﷺ said {reward}Paradise has one hundred levels{/reward}, and between each two is like the distance between earth and sky.
now: People aim for the top floor apartment, the corner office, the penthouse view. {idea}This garden is higher than any of it.{/idea} {reward}And there are levels above levels.{/reward}
old: Just getting in is enough. Why aim higher?
new: Paradise is lofty and has many levels, so it is worth striving to rise.
try: Add one extra good deed today, aiming a little higher than yesterday.

title: Its fruit hangs low, within easy reach.
subtitle: Nothing out of reach anymore
then: Al-Bara' bin 'Azib said the fruit will be {reward}close enough to reach while lying on one's bed.{/reward} More than one early scholar said the same. {idea}Nothing will need straining for.{/idea}
now: You work two jobs for things that always seem one paycheck away. You stretch for promotions that keep moving. {trap}Here, everything is just out of reach.{/trap} {reward}There, it is close.{/reward}
old: Life is always reaching for things I cannot quite get.
new: The struggle of reaching ends in a garden where everything is near.
try: When something feels out of reach today, say: Allah, make Paradise's fruit near for me.

title: Eat and drink in peace for what you sent ahead.
subtitle: The days you lived are now the meal

row.title: deeds and His mercy
sub: not even the Prophet ﷺ without it

then: Ibn Kathir calls this {reward}an invitation of blessing, favor and goodness.{/reward} The Prophet ﷺ said: work and strive, and know that {idea}none of you enters Paradise by his deeds alone{/idea}, not even me, {reward}unless Allah covers me with His mercy.{/reward}
now: The fast in summer, the night you visited the sick, the money you gave quietly. {idea}They feel like they vanish.{/idea} {reward}They are being sent ahead.{/reward} And Allah's mercy is what makes the meal.
old: My good deeds disappear into nothing.
new: What I do now is sent ahead, and Allah's mercy turns it into a feast.
try: Do one good deed today and think of it as sending a meal ahead for yourself.

title: I wish I had never been given my record.
subtitle: The regret of the left hand
then: Right after the joy of the right hand comes the other side. Ibn Kathir says this is {trap}the condition of the wretched{/trap} when the record is placed in the left hand. {trap}At this time he will be very remorseful.{/trap}
now: You open a message you dread, and wish you never had. That small feeling is a sign. {idea}The record is still being written.{/idea} {reward}You can still change what it says.{/reward}
old: I will deal with my record when the time comes.
new: My record is still open, and today I can add to it what I will be glad to read.
try: Do one thing today you would be glad to find in your record.

title: And that I had never known my account.
subtitle: Not wanting to know what you did
then: He continues: {trap}I wish I had never known how my account is.{/trap} The earlier verses said nothing will be hidden that Day. {idea}The one who never checked himself in this life{/idea} now wishes he could look away.
now: You avoid the bank app because you do not want to see the number. You skip the checkup. {trap}Not knowing feels safer.{/trap} {idea}Looking at your own deeds now is a mercy, because now you can fix them.{/idea}
old: Some things are better not to know.
new: Checking my own account now is a gift, because I can still change it.
try: Tonight, take two minutes to review your day honestly: one good, one to fix.

title: If only death had been the end.
subtitle: Wishing for the thing he once feared most

row.title: wishes for it
sub: a death with no life after

then: Ad-Dahhak said he means {trap}a death not followed by any life.{/trap} Qatadah said {trap}he will hope for death, though in the world it was the thing he hated most.{/trap}
now: Death is the thing nobody wants to talk about at dinner. You change the subject. {idea}But death is not the end of the story.{/idea} {reward}Thinking about what comes after is a way to prepare, not to fear.{/reward}
old: Death ends everything, so why think about after?
new: Death is not the end. What comes after is what I am preparing for.
try: Remember death once today, calmly, and ask Allah for a good ending.

title: My wealth did nothing for me.
subtitle: The money that could not help
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}my wealth did not protect me from the punishment of Allah.{/trap} Now {trap}the matter has ended with me alone.{/trap} The man who trusted money finds it stayed behind.
now: The savings account. The car. The investments you check every morning. {trap}You may feel they protect you.{/trap} {idea}They protect nothing on that Day, except what you gave for Allah.{/idea}
old: Money is my safety net.
new: Wealth stays behind. What I spent for Allah is what helps me.
try: Give a small amount today to someone in need, as a deposit that crosses over.

title: My power is gone from me.
subtitle: Status that disappears when it is needed

row.title: gone
sub: no helper, no one to save

row.title: on loan
sub: a test of how I use it

then: Ibn Kathir says he means {trap}my honor did not protect me{/trap}, and now {trap}I have no helper nor anyone to save me.{/trap} After wealth, he mourns his power.
now: The title on your email signature. Being the one who decides at home. The people who answer when you call. {trap}All of it can disappear.{/trap} {idea}How you use power over others is what remains.{/idea}
old: My position gives me security.
new: Power is on loan. What I did with it is what I will answer for.
try: Use whatever authority you have today to make one person's day easier.

title: Seize him and bind him.
subtitle: The end of all freedom to choose
then: Ibn Kathir says the guardians of Hell will be commanded to {trap}remove him by force from the gathering place and bind him.{/trap} The one who would not bow when free {trap}is now unable to move at all.{/trap}
now: Today you are free. You can pray or not, give or not, apologize or not. {idea}That freedom will not last forever.{/idea} {reward}The good choices you make now are made while you still can.{/reward}
old: I am free to do as I please, so why worry?
new: My freedom now is a chance to choose well, not a reason to delay.
try: Use your freedom today to choose one good thing you could easily skip.

title: Then drive him into the Fire.
subtitle: A sober warning, given so you never reach it
then: Ibn Kathir says he will be {trap}carried off and cast into Hell.{/trap} The surah introduction says these verses show the purpose of the second life: {idea}every person appears in the court of their Lord.{/idea} The warning came to Makkah while there was still time.
now: A warning sign on the highway is not cruelty. It is care for whoever reads it. {idea}This verse is a warning sign.{/idea} {reward}It is here so you can take the other road.{/reward}
old: Verses about the Fire are just meant to frighten.
new: The warning is a mercy, telling me where the road ends so I can turn.
try: Ask Allah three times today: protect me from the Fire.

title: Then bind him in a chain seventy cubits long.
subtitle: The chain of a life spent ignoring the warning
then: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Jurayj said {trap}each cubit will be the forearm length of an angel.{/trap} The verse describes the end of the man who did not believe and {trap}did not care for the poor{/trap}, as the next verses explain.
now: Habits are like links. One lie, then another to cover it. One missed prayer, then a week. {trap}Chains are built a link at a time.{/trap} {idea}They can also be broken a link at a time.{/idea}
old: One wrong choice does not matter much.
new: Choices link together. Breaking one bad link today matters.
try: Break one link in a bad chain today: skip it just once.

title: He did not believe in Allah, the Most Great.
subtitle: The first reason: neglecting Allah's right
then: Ibn Kathir explains {trap}he did not establish the right of Allah upon him{/trap}, of obedience and worship. {idea}Allah has a right on His servants that they worship Him alone{/idea} and associate nothing with Him.
now: You make time for the gym, the series, the family call. Prayer gets squeezed in the gaps, or not at all. {idea}Allah has a right on your time.{/idea} {reward}Giving it is the first thing that matters.{/reward}
old: Belief is a private feeling. It does not ask anything of me.
new: Believing in Allah, the Most Great, means giving Him His right in my life.
try: Give Allah the first five minutes of your morning tomorrow, before your phone.

title: And he never urged anyone to feed the poor.
subtitle: Not even encouraging others to give
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}he did not benefit Allah's creation nor give them their rights.{/trap} {idea}Servants have a right on each other to good treatment and help.{/idea} So Allah joined prayer and zakah, and the Prophet ﷺ near death urged prayer and care for those in one's charge.
now: You see a food drive in the group chat and scroll past. You could share the link, nudge a friend. {trap}Not even urging is its own silence.{/trap} {idea}Encouraging good is part of the good.{/idea}
old: If I cannot give much, there is nothing for me to do.
new: Even urging others to feed the hungry is part of what Allah asks.
try: Share one way to help feed people with a friend or group today.

title: No close friend for him there that Day.
subtitle: He did not care for others, and no one can care for him
then: Ibn Kathir explains there is {trap}no one who can save him{/trap}, nor any close friend or intercessor {trap}whose request would be honored.{/trap} The one who did not urge feeding the poor finds himself with no one.
now: Hundreds of contacts on your phone. Friends who would come to your wedding. {trap}None of them can stand for you that Day.{/trap} {idea}Kindness you showed others is what shows up for you.{/idea}
old: I have plenty of people who would help me.
new: On that Day, only what I did for others and for Allah stands with me.
try: Help one person today who cannot pay you back.

title: No food for him but the worst food.
subtitle: The one who withheld food from the poor

row.title: in the world
sub: did not urge feeding the poor

then: Ibn Kathir says he will have {trap}no food there except ghislin.{/trap} Qatadah said {trap}it will be the worst food of the people of the Fire.{/trap} It follows straight after the verse about not caring to feed the poor.
now: The leftovers you throw away. The extra portion you could have given. The neighbor whose fridge you never wonder about. {idea}Food is a test of sharing.{/idea} {reward}Every shared plate is a step away from this verse.{/reward}
old: What I eat and waste is my own business.
new: Food is a blessing that comes with a share for the hungry.
try: Share a meal or a plate of food with someone today.

title: Only the sinners will eat it.
subtitle: A fate reserved for those who chose wrong
then: The section closes: {trap}none will eat it except the sinners.{/trap} It ends the description of the man who {trap}neither believed nor cared for the poor.{/trap} It is not random. {idea}It follows a life of chosen wrong.{/idea}
now: The verse names who this is for, so you know it is not you if you turn back. {reward}Repentance is open right now.{/reward} {idea}The one who returns to Allah is not counted among them.{/idea}
old: These verses make me feel hopeless.
new: The warning is for those who keep choosing sin. I can choose to turn back today.
try: Make tawbah today for one specific wrong, and do one good deed after it.

title: Allah swears by everything you can see.
subtitle: The visible world as a witness
then: The second part of the surah turns to the Quran itself. Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}swears by His creation, in which His signs can be seen{/idea}, and which {reward}show the perfection of His Names and Attributes.{/reward}
now: The sunrise through the kitchen window. Your baby's fingers. The rain on the car roof. {idea}Everything you see is a witness.{/idea} The oath asks you to look again.
old: What I see every day is ordinary.
new: Everything I see is a sign of Allah, sworn by as a witness.
try: Stop once today and look closely at one ordinary thing. Say subhanAllah.

title: And by everything you cannot see.
subtitle: Most of reality is hidden from you
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah then {idea}swears by the hidden things they cannot see.{/idea} Both oaths together confirm one thing: {reward}the Quran is His Speech and revelation.{/reward}
now: Wi-Fi, gravity, the air in your lungs. You cannot see any of it, and you rely on all of it. {idea}The unseen is not unreal.{/idea} Angels, the soul, the Hereafter belong to it too.
old: If I cannot see it, I find it hard to believe.
new: Much of what is most real is unseen, and Allah swears by it.
try: Think of one unseen blessing you depend on today, and thank Allah for it.

title: This is the word of a noble Messenger.
subtitle: What the oath is sworn for
then: Ibn Kathir explains the word messenger {idea}carries the meaning of conveying{/idea}, because a messenger delivers from the sender. In Surat At-Takwir it is used for Jibril, here for {reward}Muhammad ﷺ, who carried the trust faithfully.{/reward}
now: A courier brings you a letter. You do not think the words are his. {idea}The Quran came through noble messengers{/idea}, delivered without change. {reward}It is a letter to you.{/reward}
old: The Quran is a book written by a man.
new: It is Allah's word, delivered faithfully by noble messengers.
try: Before reading Quran today, remind yourself: this is Allah speaking to me.

title: Not the word of a poet. Little do you believe.
subtitle: The verse that answered Umar's thought
then: The surah introduction tells that Umar, before Islam, stood behind the Prophet ﷺ as he recited this surah. Amazed at its beauty, Umar thought {trap}he must be a poet{/trap}, and just then he heard: {idea}it is not the word of a poet.{/idea}
now: You hear a recitation and feel it is beautiful, like a good song. {trap}It is easy to stop at the sound.{/trap} {idea}The beauty is there to carry you to the meaning.{/idea}
old: The Quran is beautiful, like great poetry.
new: Its beauty is not poetry. It is revelation, asking me to believe.
try: Listen to one short recitation today, then read its meaning.

title: Not a fortune teller either. Little do you reflect.
subtitle: The second answer that reached Umar's heart
then: Umar then thought, {trap}he must be a soothsayer, if not a poet.{/trap} The very next words recited were {idea}nor the word of a soothsayer, little do you reflect.{/idea} Umar said Islam entered deep into his heart.
now: You hear a verse that seems to answer what you were just thinking. {idea}It happens.{/idea} The question is whether you stop and reflect, {trap}or move on to the next video.{/trap}
old: I would believe more if I had more proof.
new: Often what I lack is not proof but reflection.
try: Take one verse you read today and spend five minutes thinking about it.

title: A revelation from the Lord of all the worlds.
subtitle: Where it truly comes from

row.title: revelation
sub: from the Lord of all that exists

then: After the two denials comes the positive answer. Ibn Kathir: {idea}this is the revelation sent down from the Lord of all that exists.{/idea} Umar heard this line and {reward}it stayed in his heart{/reward}, though he believed fully only later.
now: The Quran on your shelf, maybe dusty. The app you open in Ramadan. {idea}It is a message from the Lord of every world.{/idea} {reward}Some seeds take years to grow, like Umar's.{/reward}
old: I will take the Quran seriously when I feel ready.
new: It is from the Lord of the worlds, and even a little attention plants a seed.
try: Open the Quran today and read just one page.

title: Had he made up a single word about Us.
subtitle: The Messenger ﷺ could not invent a thing
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}if Muhammad ﷺ forged something against Us{/trap}, or added or removed anything from the Message, {idea}We would surely be swift in punishing him.{/idea} And of course, {reward}he did not do any of this.{/reward}
now: You pass on a quote you are not sure of. You say the Prophet ﷺ said something you saw in a forwarded message. {trap}It is easy to add to religion.{/trap} {idea}Even the Messenger ﷺ was held to exactness.{/idea}
old: Passing on a nice saying about Islam is harmless.
new: Words attributed to Allah or His Messenger ﷺ must be exact.
try: Before forwarding the next religious quote, check its source first.

title: We would have seized him by the right hand.
subtitle: The strongest grip, to show how serious it is
then: Ibn Kathir says it has been explained that the right hand is mentioned {idea}because it is stronger in grabbing.{/idea} The point is that {reward}Allah Himself guarded the message{/reward}, and the Prophet ﷺ was truthful.
now: You wonder sometimes if what you read was changed over time. {reward}Allah guarded this message from the start{/reward}, even from the one who brought it. {idea}You can trust what you hold.{/idea}
old: Maybe the message was changed along the way.
new: Allah guarded the message so firmly that even its Messenger ﷺ could not alter it.
try: Thank Allah today for preserving the Quran you can open on your phone.

title: Then We would have cut his life artery.
subtitle: The certainty that he spoke only truth
then: Ibn Abbas said al-watin is {idea}the artery attached to the heart.{/idea} Ibn Kathir sums it up: the point is that {reward}he ﷺ is truthful, righteous and guided{/reward}, and Allah helped him with clear proofs.
now: People trust a doctor who has never been caught lying. {reward}The Messenger ﷺ conveyed the message to the end and was never stopped.{/reward} {idea}That itself is a sign of who sent him.{/idea}
old: How can I be sure the Prophet ﷺ spoke the truth?
new: Allah said He would have stopped any lie at once. He never did.
try: Read one hadith about the Prophet's honesty today and share it with someone.

title: And none of you could have shielded him.
subtitle: No one stands between Allah and His decision
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}none of you would be able to come between Us and him{/trap} if We wanted it. The deniers could not have protected him. {idea}And because no one could stop Allah, his safety proved his truth.{/idea}
now: You think the right connections will protect you. The lawyer, the uncle with influence. {trap}No one can stand between you and Allah.{/trap} {idea}So seek protection from Him directly.{/idea}
old: With the right people behind me, I am safe.
new: No one can shield me from Allah. Only He can protect me.
try: Say a short du'a for protection this morning instead of relying only on people.

title: It is a reminder for those mindful of Allah.
subtitle: Who the Quran actually reaches
then: Ibn Kathir says the Quran is a reminder for the mindful, and cites: {reward}it is for those who believe a guide and a healing{/reward}, and for those who disbelieve {trap}there is heaviness in their ears.{/trap}
now: Two people hear the same verse on the same radio. One stops and thinks, one changes the station. {idea}The difference is the heart.{/idea} {reward}A little taqwa opens the ears.{/reward}
old: The Quran does not seem to affect me much.
new: The more mindful of Allah I am, the more the Quran reaches me.
try: Before reading or listening to Quran today, ask Allah to open your heart to it.

title: We know some among you will still deny.
subtitle: Clarity does not force belief
then: Ibn Kathir explains that even {idea}with this explanation and clarification{/idea}, there will still be {trap}those who reject the Quran.{/trap} Allah knew it, and told His Messenger ﷺ so.
now: You share a reminder with your family and someone rolls their eyes. You explain your faith to a coworker and it goes nowhere. {idea}Allah already knew some would deny.{/idea} {reward}Your task is to be sincere, not to convince everyone.{/reward}
old: If people do not accept what I share, I failed.
new: Some will deny however clear it is. My part is to share sincerely.
try: Share one good reminder today and let go of how it is received.

title: It will be deep regret for those who reject it.
subtitle: The Quran ignored becomes a sorrow
then: Ibn Jarir said {trap}this rejection will be anguish for the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment.{/trap} Ibn Kathir adds it may refer to the Quran itself, and cites: {trap}a barrier will be set between them and what they desire.{/trap}
now: The course you never took. The call you never returned. {trap}Regret is for chances missed.{/trap} {reward}The Quran is a chance in your hand right now.{/reward}
old: I can always come back to the Quran later.
new: The Quran I ignore now could become my regret. The Quran I follow becomes my guide.
try: Set a small daily Quran time, even five minutes, starting today.

title: It is the certain truth.
subtitle: No doubt, suspicion, or confusion in it
then: Ibn Kathir says it is {idea}the right and truthful news in which there is no doubt, suspicion or confusion.{/idea} The surah began with al-Haqqah, the inevitable reality, and {reward}closes by calling the Quran the certain truth.{/reward}
now: Headlines change by the hour. Experts reverse themselves. Your feed contradicts itself before lunch. {trap}Certainty is rare.{/trap} {reward}Here is a book with none of that doubt.{/reward}
old: Nothing can really be known for certain.
new: The Quran is truth I can stand on when everything else shifts.
try: When you feel unsure today, read one verse and let it steady you.

title: So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great.
subtitle: The fitting response to all that was said

row.title: close the book and move on

then: Ibn Kathir says this means glorify {idea}the One Who sent down this magnificent Quran.{/idea} After the Day of Judgment, the records, and the truth of the message, {reward}the surah ends with praise.{/reward}
now: You finish a powerful talk and immediately check your phone. {trap}The moment passes.{/trap} {reward}This verse asks you to end with your Lord's name on your tongue.{/reward}
old: After reading, I just move on with my day.
new: The right ending to hearing the truth is glorifying the One who sent it.
try: Say subhana Rabbiyal 'Azim slowly three times right now, then in each ruku' today.
